content: Please refer to the product packaging for the medication you are taking. If you are self-treating and your symptoms of acid-related issues persist or worsen after two weeks of using this product, or if you suspect a serious medical condition, seek medical attention immediately. If you are using this medication daily for more than two weeks, it may indicate an underlying medical issue requiring alternative treatment. If your doctor has prescribed this medication for acidosis or to alkalinize your urine, the dosage will depend on your specific medical condition and response to treatment. To maximize the benefits of this medication, take it regularly and exactly as directed. It is typically taken orally several times a day. To help you remember, take it at the same times each day. Side Effects: Nausea, bloating, or gas may occur. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. When taken with sodium bicarbonate, consuming large amounts of calcium from your diet, medications, or supplements can rarely lead to a serious condition called milk-alkali syndrome. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about the safe use of calcium products while on this medication. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking sodium bicarbonate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may also pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication can reduce the effectiveness of certain drugs that require stomach acid to work, such as ampicillin, atazanavir, certain azole antifungals (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), iron supplements, pazopanib, sucralfate, and others. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (usually 81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise by your doctor. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., calcium, potassium, sodium, or bicarbonate levels) should be performed if you are taking high doses or using this medication for more than two weeks. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
